Subject: Math
Summary (EN): Students construct 3D towers using pictures of front and side views.

10 snap cubes per student, in 4 colours (yellow = 1 unit tall, green = 2, blue = 3, pink/red = 4)
Printed game boards (4 × 4 and 5 × 5 grids; Appendix B)
Warm-up slide deck (Appendix A), projected in edit mode

Gr 6 E1.2: draw top, front, and side views, as well as perspective views, of objects and physical spaces, using appropriate scales

Subject: Math
Summary (EN): Students apply right‑angle trigonometry to estimate and calculate the width of a simulated river.
Summary (FR): Les élèves appliquent la trigonométrie du triangle rectangle pour estimer et calculer la largeur d'une rivière simulée.
Materials (EN):
Trig River worksheet, 1 per student
Protractor, or the printable paper half-protractor, 1 per pair
Tape measure (at least 5 m) and masking tape
A 'river' 2–5 m wide: two parallel lines (sidewalk, field lines, or rows of desks)
Materials (FR):
Fiche « Trig River », 1 par élève
Rapporteur ou demi-rapporteur en papier imprimable, 1 par dyade
Ruban à mesurer (au moins 5 m) et ruban-cache
Une « rivière » de 2 à 5 m : deux lignes parallèles (trottoir, lignes de terrain ou rangées de pupitres)

Gr 10 MPM2D Trigonometry 2: solve problems involving right triangles, using the primary trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean theorem
Gr 9 MTH1W E1.5: solve problems involving the side-length relationship for right triangles in real-life situations, including problems that involve composite shapes

Subject: Science
Summary (EN): Students sketch the changing shadow of an object over time to explore how the position of the sun (or Earth’s rotation) affects shadow direction, length, and shape.

Large paper or a paved surface for chalk
Pencil or chalk
A small object (toy figure or block) or a stick
Clock or timer

Grande feuille ou surface pavée pour la craie
Crayon ou craie
Petit objet (figurine ou bloc) ou bâton

Title (EN): Exploring Light with Optics (Design Challenge: Laser Maze)
Title (FR): Explorer la lumière avec l'optique (défi de conception : labyrinthe laser)
Subject: Science
Spatial skills: Perspective Taking; Visualization; Mental Rotation; Visuospatial Manipulation
Summary (EN): Part of a comprehensive unit plan designed the Perimeter Institute, this activity (p.52-60) invites students use their knowledge of reflection and refraction to build and solve laser mazes. While originally designed for Grade 10 students, this activity can adapted for use in younger grades using reflection only.
Summary (FR): Tiré d'une unité du Perimeter Institute (p. 52–60), cette activité invite les élèves à utiliser la réflexion et la réfraction pour construire et résoudre des labyrinthes laser. Conçue pour la 10e année, elle peut être adaptée aux plus jeunes en utilisant seulement la réflexion.
Materials (EN):
Per group: 1 laser pointer (Class 2, under 1 mW)
4–6 mirror squares (or foil on cardboard)
Binder clips and modelling clay to stand mirrors upright
Shallow cardboard box
Tape, protractor, paper and pencils
Materials (FR):
Par groupe : 1 pointeur laser (classe 2, moins de 1 mW)
4 à 6 miroirs carrés (ou papier d'aluminium sur carton)
Pinces à reliure et pâte à modeler pour maintenir les miroirs
Boîte de carton peu profonde
Ruban adhésif, rapporteur, papier et crayons
Teacher notes: Review laser safety: never point at eyes or reflective surfaces near faces.
Ontario science expectations:
Gr 10 SNC2D E2.2: use an inquiry process to investigate the laws of reflection, using plane and curved mirrors, and draw ray diagrams
Gr 10 SNC2D E2.4: use an inquiry process to investigate the refraction of light as it passes through media of different refractive indices
Science thinking processes: Engineering design process; Scientific experimentation process

Title (EN): Exploring Light with Optics (Activity Stations: Activity 1 - How Do We See?)
Title (FR): Explorer la lumière avec l'optique (stations : Comment voyons-nous?)
Subject: Science
Spatial skills: Visualization; Schematizing; Multiple Representations; Mental Rotation
Summary (EN): Part of a comprehensive unit plan designed the Perimeter Institute, this hands-on station activity (p.13 -23), students investigate several optical principles that underlie how our eyes work by exploring six topics: how the eye uses a converging lens, how the eye sees objects at varying distances (accommodation), how the pupils work, how peripheral vision works, how to locate the eye’s blind spot, and why we have two eyes. These quick activities at different stations are supported by station cards and a student activity sheet.
Summary (FR): Tirée d'une unité du Perimeter Institute (p. 13–23), cette activité en stations permet d'étudier les principes optiques de la vision : lentille convergente, accommodation, pupille, vision périphérique, tache aveugle et vision binoculaire.
Materials (EN):
Stations 1–3: lenses, light sources and lab equipment (see unit; needs advance preparation)
Stations 4–6: pen, paper, metre stick, tape, whiteboard
Station cards and student activity sheet (in unit)
Materials (FR):
Stations 1 à 3 : lentilles, sources lumineuses et matériel de laboratoire (voir l'unité; préparation requise)
Stations 4 à 6 : stylo, papier, règle d'un mètre, ruban adhésif, tableau blanc
Cartes de station et fiche de l'élève (dans l'unité)
Teacher notes: Stations 4–6 work on their own if lab equipment isn't available.
Ontario science expectations: Gr 10 SNC2D E3.5: describe the characteristics and positions of images formed by converging lenses, using ray diagrams

Title (FR): Jeu de rôle du cycle du carbone
Subject: Science

Student worksheet

Title (EN): Using maps and investigating catch rates to understand lobster abundance in Nova Scotia waters
